flowers-programs-music.whatItIs: Choosing flowers, printed programs and music for the service.
flowers-programs-music.whyItMatters: These small choices help the service feel like the person. The funeral home has to give you a written price list, and you can buy goods and services separately.
flowers-programs-music.whoToCall: The funeral home, a florist, or the place where the service will be held.
flowers-programs-music.doesNotApplyWhen: There is no service, or the family wants to keep it plain.

guest-book.whatItIs: A book where guests sign their names and leave a short note.
guest-book.whyItMatters: It shows you later who came. Some people find comfort in reading it in the months after.
guest-book.whoToCall: The funeral home may have one. A plain notebook also works.

reception.whatItIs: A gathering after the service, sometimes called a repast. You choose the place, the food and who hosts.
reception.whyItMatters: It gives people time to talk and share memories. It can be small.
reception.whoToCall: A friend, family member or faith community who can host. They can also help with the food.
reception.doesNotApplyWhen: The family does not want a gathering after the service.

eulogy.whatItIs: A short talk about the person's life, given at the service.
eulogy.whyItMatters: It helps people remember who the person was. Someone close to them can give it, or you can.
eulogy.whoToCall: A family member, a close friend, or the person leading the service.
eulogy.doesNotApplyWhen: There is no service, or the person leading it will speak for the family.

family-transport.whatItIs: Getting close family to the service, the burial and the reception.
family-transport.whyItMatters: On the day, people may be too tired or upset to drive. A plan takes one worry away.
family-transport.whoToCall: The funeral home, or friends who offer to drive.
family-transport.doesNotApplyWhen: Everyone can get there on their own.

notify-community.whatItIs: Telling the person's employer, clergy, and any clubs or groups they belonged to.
notify-community.whyItMatters: These people may want to come to the service or help the family.
notify-community.whoToCall: The employer's human resources office, the person's place of worship, and group leaders.
notify-community.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no employer or groups to tell.

notify-ssa.whatItIs: Letting Social Security know about the death.
notify-ssa.whyItMatters: Social Security benefits stop at death, and Social Security tells Medicare. A payment for the month of death goes back to Social Security.
notify-ssa.whoToCall: Often the funeral director reports the death for you. Give them the person's Social Security number, and ask them if they did it. If not, call Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 (TTY 1-800-325-0778) or visit a local office. They take death reports only by phone or in person.
notify-ssa.whatToBring: The person's Social Security number. You can start without the death certificate, but they will need it later.

notify-banks.whatItIs: Telling banks, credit card companies, credit bureaus and other financial companies about the death.
notify-banks.whyItMatters: If Social Security paid by direct deposit, ask the bank to send back the payment for the month of death and any later ones.
notify-banks.whoToCall: Each bank and card company, and the credit bureaus.
notify-banks.whatToBring: Certified copies of the death certificate.
notify-banks.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no accounts or cards.

life-insurance-claims.whatItIs: Telling each life insurance company about the death and asking for a claim.
life-insurance-claims.whyItMatters: The money can help with funeral costs and bills. Someone needs to ask each company for it.
life-insurance-claims.whoToCall: Each insurance company. Look at the policy, or ask the person's employer if they had insurance through work. If the person was a veteran, the VA can tell you about veterans life insurance.
life-insurance-claims.whatToBring: A certified copy of the death certificate, and the policy number if you have it.
life-insurance-claims.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no life insurance.

pension-retirement.whatItIs: Telling the person's pension or retirement plan about the death.
pension-retirement.whyItMatters: Payments to the person stop. For a military retiree, DFAS stops the monthly payments and sends Survivor Benefit Plan forms if the person was enrolled.
pension-retirement.whoToCall: The plan's office or the former employer. For a military retiree, contact the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS). For a VA pension, contact the VA.
pension-retirement.whatToBring: A certified copy of the death certificate.
pension-retirement.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no pension or retirement plan.

utilities-housing.whatItIs: Telling the power, water, gas and phone companies, and the landlord or mortgage holder.
utilities-housing.whyItMatters: Bills keep coming until someone tells them. Rules for leases and mortgages vary by state.
utilities-housing.whoToCall: Each utility company, the landlord, and the mortgage company.
utilities-housing.doesNotApplyWhen: Someone else in the home already pays these bills in their own name.

cancel-subscriptions.whatItIs: Stopping memberships, streaming services, gym plans and other things that charge every month.
cancel-subscriptions.whyItMatters: These charges keep going until someone stops them.
cancel-subscriptions.whoToCall: Each company. Bank and card statements show what charges each month.
cancel-subscriptions.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no recurring charges.

forward-mail.whatItIs: Having the person's mail sent to the person who handles their affairs.
forward-mail.whyItMatters: Mail shows bills, accounts and benefits you may not know about.
forward-mail.whoToCall: The post office. To forward all of their mail, the executor or administrator goes to a post office in person.
forward-mail.whatToBring: Proof that you are the appointed executor or administrator. A death certificate alone is not enough.
forward-mail.doesNotApplyWhen: You lived with the person. You can open and manage their mail at that address.

thank-you-notes.whatItIs: Short notes to people who sent flowers, gave to a cause, brought food or helped.
thank-you-notes.whyItMatters: They let people know their kindness reached you. There is no deadline, and a few words are enough.
thank-you-notes.doesNotApplyWhen: You do not feel ready. A friend or family member can help write them.

will-and-probate.whatItIs: Finding out what to do with the will, and whether the estate needs to go through probate.
will-and-probate.whyItMatters: The executor settles the person's debts from the estate. Family members usually do not pay those debts from their own money.
will-and-probate.whoToCall: A probate lawyer, the county court or a tax preparer can tell you what applies.
will-and-probate.whatToBring: The will if there is one, a certified copy of the death certificate, and a list of what the person owned and owed.

retitle-property.whatItIs: Moving homes, vehicles and accounts into a living person's name.
retitle-property.whyItMatters: Homes, vehicles and accounts stay in the person's name until someone transfers them. For a vehicle, the state motor vehicles office can transfer the title and cancel the person's license or ID.
retitle-property.whoToCall: A probate lawyer, the county court or a tax preparer can tell you what applies.
retitle-property.whatToBring: Certified copies of the death certificate, and the title or account papers.
retitle-property.doesNotApplyWhen: The person owned nothing in their own name.

online-accounts.whatItIs: Closing or saving the person's email, social media and other online accounts.
online-accounts.whyItMatters: Some families keep a social media page as a place to remember. Others close the accounts.
online-accounts.whoToCall: Each company. Look in its help pages for what to do when an account holder dies.
online-accounts.doesNotApplyWhen: The person had no online accounts.

final-tax-return.whatItIs: The person's last income tax return. It reports all income up to the date of death.
final-tax-return.whyItMatters: The usual tax deadlines apply. If a refund is due, someone has to claim it. If the person did not file for earlier years, those returns may be needed too.
final-tax-return.whoToCall: A probate lawyer, the county court or a tax preparer can tell you what applies. The IRS calls the person who files the personal representative: an executor, an administrator, or anyone else in charge of the person's property. A surviving spouse can file a joint return.
final-tax-return.whatToBring: The person's tax papers and income records. The IRS does not need a copy of the death certificate.

headstone.whatItIs: Ordering a headstone or grave marker for the burial place.
headstone.whyItMatters: It marks where the person rests, so family can visit.
headstone.whoToCall: The cemetery, or a monument maker. If the person was a veteran, the VA may provide a headstone or marker. Call the VA at 800-697-6947.
headstone.whatToBring: For a VA headstone: VA Form 40-1330 and a copy of the veteran's discharge papers. Do not send original papers.
headstone.doesNotApplyWhen: The person was cremated and the family is not using a grave or niche marker.

follow-up-claims.whatItIs: Checking on insurance and benefit claims that are still open.
follow-up-claims.whyItMatters: Some claims have time limits. A spouse and minor children may be able to get Social Security survivor benefits. For a veteran, a VA burial allowance claim is usually due within 2 years after the burial, with some exceptions.
follow-up-claims.whoToCall: Each insurance company, Social Security at 1-800-772-1213, and the VA at 800-827-1000 if the person was a veteran.
follow-up-claims.whatToBring: Claim numbers, letters you received, and a certified copy of the death certificate.
follow-up-claims.doesNotApplyWhen: All claims are paid or closed.
